# Configuration

## How configuration works

TTpipe is driven by two kinds of files, as in dietJuicer:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `samplesheet.txt` | One row per sample |
| `config/TTpipeConfig.yaml` | Everything else: reference, switches, processing parameters, DESeq2, GSEA, QC cut-offs |

`--configfile other.yaml` on the launcher replaces it; make that file a complete
copy, because the launcher reads `hpcProfile` and `outputDir` from it. The shipped
file is commented line by line; this chapter is the full reference. No path, name
or parameter is written into the Snakefiles. The defaults reproduce the guide's
workflow unless a comment in the file says "TTpipe change".

```yaml
samplesheet: 'samplesheet.txt'
run_processing: true
run_analysis: true
qc_report: true
multiqc: true
multiqc_extra: ''
analysis_counts: ''
hpcProfile: 'profiles/local'
outputDir: 'output'
genome: 'mm10'
genome_fasta: '/path/to/GRCm38.primary_assembly.genome.fa'
gtf: '/path/to/gencode.vM25.annotation.gtf'
star_index: '/path/to/mm10_STARgenome'
build_star_index: false
sjdb_overhang: 100
notify: {email: '', events: ['start', 'success', 'error'], command: 'mail -s {subject} {email}'}
trim: false
fastp_extra: ''
star_extra: ''
min_mapq: 10
remove_duplicates: true
picard_extra: ''
strandedness: 'dUTP'
scale_factors: {}
bigwig_bin_size: 50
bigwig_extra: ''
sample_tracks: false
htseq_feature: 'gene'
htseq_id_attribute: 'gene_id'
htseq_nonunique: 'all'
count_strand: 'sum'
reference_condition: 'DMSO'
condition_order: []
comparisons: []
design: '~ condition + replicate'
min_count: 10
min_samples: 2
alpha: 0.01
lfc_threshold: 0
gsea_collections: {}
gsea_min_size: 1
gsea_max_size: 1000000
gsea_seed: 42
qc_thresholds: {...}
```

## Samples

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `samplesheet` | `samplesheet.txt` | Path to the tab-separated sample table ([Setup](setup.qmd#samplesheet)) |

## What to run

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `run_processing` | `true` | FASTQ to BAM, tracks and counts. When false, no FASTQ columns are needed |
| `run_analysis` | `true` | DESeq2, GSEA, Sankey |
| `qc_report` | `true` | Per-sample QC table and `TTpipe_qc_report.html` |
| `multiqc` | `true` | Also `TTpipe_multiqc.html` (FastQC, fastp, STAR, Picard). Only on processing runs |
| `multiqc_extra` | `''` | Extra arguments passed to `multiqc` |
| `analysis_counts` | `''` | For `run_processing: false`: path to an existing count matrix (tab-separated, first column `gene_id`, header = sample `Name`s). Empty = use this pipeline's `counts/counts_deseq2.txt` |

If all of `run_processing`, `run_analysis` and `qc_report` are false the workflow
stops with "nothing to do". With `run_processing: false`, `run_analysis: true` and
no counts anywhere, it stops with a message asking for `analysis_counts`.

## Compute site and output

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `hpcProfile` | `profiles/local` | Profile folder (with `env.sh` and `config.yaml`). Overridden by `--profile` and `$TTPIPE_PROFILE` |
| `outputDir` | `output` | Where results go. A relative path is placed under `$TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT` if set, else the folder you launch from. `~` is expanded. An absolute path is used as written |

## Reference

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `genome` | `mm10` | A label only (shown in the QC report header) |
| `genome_fasta` | placeholder path | Genome FASTA; read only when building the STAR index. **Must match the GTF's chromosome names** |
| `gtf` | placeholder path | Unzipped GTF: used by the STAR index, HTSeq and the gene table |
| `star_index` | placeholder path | STAR genome directory. If empty and `build_star_index` is true: `<outputDir>/reference/star_index`. If empty and the index is not being built, the workflow stops |
| `build_star_index` | `false` | `true`: build the index from `genome_fasta` and `gtf` (once; roughly 32 GB of memory or more, a starting guess) |
| `sjdb_overhang` | `100` | `STAR --sjdbOverhang` at index build: read length minus 1. Passed explicitly (the guide uses STAR's default, 100) |

## Notifications

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `notify.email` | `''` | Address for start, finish and failure emails. `$TTPIPE_EMAIL` wins if set; with neither, nothing is sent |
| `notify.events` | `['start', 'success', 'error']` | Which events send a message |
| `notify.command` | `mail -s {subject} {email}` | Shell command that sends one message; `{subject}` and `{email}` are filled in (shell-quoted) and the body arrives on stdin. Use e.g. `sendmail {email}` and put a `Subject:` line in the body if your cluster has no `mail` |

One email at start, one at the end, one if any job fails (with the last 40 lines
of the Snakemake log); not one per job; none on dry runs. A failure to send
only prints a message.

## Processing

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `trim` | `false` | Trim with fastp before STAR. The guide runs FastQC only |
| `fastp_extra` | `''` | Extra fastp arguments |
| `star_extra` | `''` | Extra STAR arguments (the guide uses STAR's defaults) |
| `min_mapq` | `10` | `samtools view -q`. STAR's unique reads have MAPQ 255 |
| `remove_duplicates` | `true` | Picard `REMOVE_DUPLICATES`; `false` only marks them |
| `picard_extra` | `''` | Extra Picard arguments, e.g. `VALIDATION_STRINGENCY=LENIENT` |
| `strandedness` | `dUTP` | `dUTP` (read 1 antisense, read 2 sense) or `forward` (read 1 sense). Any other value stops the workflow |

STAR is always run with `--outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate --readFilesCommand
zcat --quantMode GeneCounts` and a per-sample `--outTmpDir`; `star_extra` is
added.

## Tracks (bigWig)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `scale_factors` | `{}` | Per-condition overrides, e.g. `{DMSO: 1.2757, 2H: 1}`. Listed conditions use your value; the rest are computed as (largest merged-replicate mapped-pair count) / (this condition's). [Recipe](recipes.qmd#pinning-scale-factors) |
| `bigwig_bin_size` | `50` | `bamCoverage --binSize` (also deepTools' own default) |
| `bigwig_extra` | `''` | Extra `bamCoverage` arguments |
| `sample_tracks` | `false` | Also one bigWig set per sample. [Recipe](recipes.qmd#per-sample-tracks) |

Mapped pairs are BAM records divided by two, on the replicate-merged all-reads
BAMs. `bamCoverage` gets `--scaleFactor` and nothing else for normalisation.

## Gene counts (HTSeq)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `htseq_feature` | `gene` | `htseq-count --type`. `gene` counts the whole gene body, introns included: the key difference from an RNA-seq count. (The gene table is always built from the GTF's `gene` lines, whatever this is.) |
| `htseq_id_attribute` | `gene_id` | `--idattr`; also the id attribute `gene_info.py` uses |
| `htseq_nonunique` | `all` | `--nonunique`. `all` counts a read that overlaps several genes for each of them |
| `count_strand` | `sum` | `sum`: forward + reverse per gene (the guide's code). `sense`: forward for + genes, reverse for - genes (the guide's text). [Recipe](recipes.qmd#counting-on-the-sense-strand-only) |

HTSeq is run with `-f bam --stranded no --order pos` on each strand BAM; other
options stay at HTSeq's defaults (for example `--mode union`).

## Differential expression (DESeq2)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `reference_condition` | `DMSO` (in the shipped file; code default: the first condition) | Control `Condition`; the base level and the default reference |
| `condition_order` | `[]` | Order of conditions in plots and the Sankey; must list exactly the samplesheet conditions. Empty = order of appearance |
| `comparisons` | `[]` | `[treatment, reference]` pairs. Empty = every other condition against `reference_condition`. Result names: `<treatment>_vs_<reference>` |
| `design` | `~ condition + replicate` | DESeq2 design. Only `condition` and `replicate` are available; `condition` is required |
| `min_count` | `10` | Prefilter: keep genes with at least this many counts... |
| `min_samples` | `2` | ...in at least this many samples |
| `alpha` | `0.01` | Adjusted p-value cut-off (results and the Sankey) |
| `lfc_threshold` | `0` | `lfcThreshold` in `results()`. 0 = none, as in the guide. Above 0, `stat` changes meaning ([Differential expression and GSEA](analysis.qmd#how-to-read-a-results-table)) |

## GSEA

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `gsea_collections` | `{}` | `{Name: '/path/to/sets.gmt'}`. Empty = GSEA is skipped. Names go into file names |
| `gsea_min_size` | `1` | Smallest gene set kept (guide: 0, no filter) |
| `gsea_max_size` | `1000000` | Largest gene set kept (guide: no filter) |
| `gsea_seed` | `42` | Random seed (the guide uses a time stamp) |

## QC thresholds {#qc-thresholds}

`qc_thresholds` maps a metric to `{direction, warn, fail}`. For
`higher_is_better` a value below `fail` fails and below `warn` warns; for
`lower_is_better` the reverse. A value exactly on a limit is not penalised.

| Metric | Direction | warn | fail |
|--------|-----------|------|------|
| `input_pairs_million` | higher | 20 | 5 |
| `unique_pct` | higher | 70 | 50 |
| `multi_pct` | lower | 15 | 30 |
| `too_short_pct` | lower | 20 | 40 |
| `duplicate_pct` | lower | 40 | 50 |
| `sense_pct` | higher | 90 | 75 |
| `rrna_pct` | lower | 5 | 15 |
| `replicate_correlation` | higher | 0.95 | 0.85 |

The `warn` values for unique, multi, too-short and duplication follow the guide's
rules of thumb; **the `fail` values and the others are TTpipe defaults, not
published standards.** See [Reading the QC report](qc.qmd).

There is also an optional key that is not in the shipped file: `qc_report_banner`
(text shown in a banner at the top of the report; the tests use it to label
synthetic data).

## Environment variables

Set in `~/.bashrc`, outside git (details in [Cluster reference](cluster.qmd#environment-variables)):
`TTPIPE_PROFILE`, `TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT`, `TTPIPE_EMAIL`, `TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT`.

## Deliberate changes from the source guide {#deliberate-changes-from-the-source-guide}

TTpipe reimplements the TT-seq workflow described in a pipeline guide for
Magnitov et al. 2024 (*Mol Cell*, doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2024.11.031; GEO GSE260914;
the authors' code is at <https://github.com/magnitov/zfp143>). It is not the
authors' code. This table lists what TTpipe does differently on purpose; each row
was checked against the code.

| # | Topic | Guide | TTpipe |
|---|-------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Reference | An Ensembl FASTA (chromosomes `1`, `2`, `X`) paired with a GENCODE GTF (`chr1`...), whose names do not match | FASTA and GTF must come from the same source (default: GENCODE vM25 GTF with a chr-prefixed FASTA). TTpipe does not check this |
| 2 | Strandedness | dUTP hard-coded | Config key `strandedness` (`dUTP` or `forward`), checked by the QC report's sense % |
| 3 | Count strand | Text and code disagree | `count_strand`: `sum` (forward + reverse, the guide's code, default) or `sense` (the guide's text) |
| 4 | Scale factors | Hard-coded | Computed, (max / this) over merged-replicate mapped pairs (records / 2); optional per-condition override |
| 5 | DESeq2 variable | `time` | Renamed `condition`; `design` validated; count columns matched to samples by name |
| 6 | VST | `vst()` | Falls back to `varianceStabilizingTransformation()` below 1000 genes |
| 7 | DEG tables | Space-delimited | CSV with a `gene_id` column |
| 8 | GSEA | Java GSEA 4.3.2; time-stamp seed; 10000 permutations; ranked by `gene_id` | fgsea; fixed seed; adaptive multilevel p-values; ranked by gene symbol (largest \|stat\| kept for duplicates). Similar in kind, not identical; never compared here |
| 9 | Sankey | Plotting code not runnable as written | Rewritten to run; a bar chart with one comparison |
| 10 | BAM merges and counting | An extra sort after each merge; one HTSeq call for all BAMs | Merges skip the redundant sort; a one-sample condition is copied; HTSeq per sample and strand (same counts, parallel) |
| 11 | Software and optional steps | FastQC only for read QC | One conda environment per rule group; optional fastp (off by default); optional MultiQC |
| 12 | QC | Not part of the guide | Extra static QC report |

Smaller differences: `--sjdbOverhang`, `--binSize` and HTSeq `--idattr` are
passed explicitly (at the same values as the defaults); STAR gets a per-sample
`--outTmpDir`; `min_mapq` and `remove_duplicates` are config keys; per-sample
tracks, email notifications and the launcher are additions.

**What TTpipe keeps from the guide:** STAR defaults with `--quantMode GeneCounts`;
MAPQ >= 10; Picard `REMOVE_DUPLICATES=true`; HTSeq `--type gene --nonunique all
--stranded no --order pos` on strand-split BAMs; `bamCoverage --scaleFactor`;
DESeq2 with `~ condition + replicate` (the guide's `~ time + replicate`),
alpha 0.01, no log2 fold-change threshold and a prefilter of at least 10 counts
in at least 2 samples; ranking by the Wald statistic; the Up / Down / n.s.
Sankey categories.
